name: Cheesy Zucchini Beef and Rice Skillet
intro_html: This is a cozy, cheesy skillet that stretches four pounds of beef across 14 hearty dinners. Taco seasoned beef, soft zucchini, and melty cheddar come together over rice for a meal that tastes like comfort food but eats like a budget win. One pan, big batch, and a fridge full of dinners waiting for you.
ingredients_display: Vegetable Oil (Great Value): 2 tbsp canola oil (40 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 5.5 cups dry: ~$1.23. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Vegetable Oil, 2 tbsp canola oil: ~$0.10. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Pantry seasonings (taco seasoning, salt, black pepper): ~$0.44. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $38.89 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.78 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $41.36 across 14 servings, roughly $2.95 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $7.86 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $49.22. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $3.52 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Watch for markdowns on lean ground beef. Buy it when it hits a low price per pound, then brown and freeze what you are not using today. Browned beef freezes great and thaws fast for the next batch.
Skip the seasoning packet and mix your own. Chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and paprika from your pantry cost pennies per batch compared to the little envelopes, and you control the salt.

Zucchini is cheapest in summer, so buy it in season. When it is not, frozen zucchini or an extra can of tomatoes fills the same role. Store brand canned tomatoes and cheese save you real money here too.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Rinse the rice and cook it according to the package. Set it aside to steam while you build the skillet.
Heat a large skillet over medium high heat with a little of the vegetable oil. Add the lean ground beef and brown it, breaking it apart as it cooks until there is no more pink.
Stir in the diced yellow onion, green bell peppers, and minced garlic with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until they start to soften.
Add the diced zucchini, the taco seasoning, the beef broth, and the canned diced tomatoes with their juice. Stir it all together so the seasoning coats everything.
Let it simmer 5 to 7 minutes until the zucchini is tender and the broth cooks down to coat everything.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fat free cheddar until it melts into the mix. Serve over the cooked rice, or fold the rice right into the skillet.
portion_html: Once everything is combined, weigh the full pot again and subtract the empty pot weight you noted at the start. Divide that total by 14 to find the target weight per container, then scoop and check each one on the scale. Even portions keep every dinner satisfying and your macros honest.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Confessions of a Fit Foodie, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Fourteen filling dinners out of one skillet, every one warm, cheesy, and easy on the wallet. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
